A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MythTriage study. Their main text, tables, equations, figures, Appendices A–I, and annotation-guideline images are readable and matchable despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original expert annotations, model evaluations, and analyses of myth prevalence, recommendation transitions, and engagement in collected YouTube data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparisons and supplementary evaluations and analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o teacher, DeBERTa student, inputs, training approaches, and deferral strategies remain unchanged. Section 5.3 explicitly states that MSP+VET defers when either condition holds; this clarifies the existing combination without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both use the same eight myths, eight topics, 73 queries, 2,893 search results, and 342,707 recommendations. The gold-standard dataset and recommendation-validation coverage are retained. New Table 2 summarizes existing datasets.

E2.justification: The ten evaluated LLMs, DeBERTa and triage comparisons, alternative deferral methods, data-balancing comparators, and GPT-4o versus GPT-4.1 stance comparison retain the same membership.

E3.justification: Both retain 305 evaluation videos per myth after excluding five demonstrations, the 80:20 synthetic training/validation split, the same prompting and training settings, and the 100-video recommendation check. Added documentation does not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The data-balancing experiment, deferral comparison, additional recommendation validation, cost analysis, and supplementary corpus analyses are retained. Appendix C.1's added metadata-ablation discussion concerns prior work and explicitly says those ablations were not rerun.

E5.justification: Annotator-agreement reporting, performance summaries with dispersion values, and Appendix I.4's statistical tests and multiple-comparison adjustment remain unchanged. No new repeated-run, seed, or confidence-interval reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Model scores, prevalence findings, and cost estimates remain unchanged. v2 newly reports a mean video duration of 7.17 minutes in Section 4.2 and corrects the comment-count effect size from the malformed η²=0.0.006 to η²=0.006 in Appendix I.4, without changing the significance finding.

T1.justification: The myth-bias definition and mathematical calculations are retained. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: scalable OUD-myth detection, reduced labeling costs, an expert-labeled dataset, and a large-scale YouTube analysis. Added context does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly identifies Google Trends sampling bias toward mainstream queries and possible underrepresentation of vulnerable populations. It also expands qualifications about error propagation and the costs of multimodal or larger models. Appendix C.1 adds a rationale for retaining all text metadata.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future-release promise with explicit code/data and model access URLs. It also specifies annotator qualifications and annotation duration, the student's parameter count, and the combined deferral rule. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit contrast with benchmark-focused cascading research. v2 also adds Chandra et al. (2025) and two YouTube-policy references. Consolidated ElSherief bibliography entries represent the same previously cited works, not removed research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose expansions and grammatical corrections, updates affiliations and correspondence information, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 summarizing existing dataset and annotation counts. Other tables are renumbered and figures and tables shift position with text reflow; the existing visualizations and appendix guideline images are retained.

improvement.justification: Resource links, clearer annotator and deferral documentation, and explicit sampling limitations modestly improve reproducibility and interpretation. The scientific evaluation remains essentially unchanged. New Table 2 misleadingly describes all recommendation annotations as GPT-4o-labeled despite Section 5.4's selective deferral; this local inconsistency tempers but does not outweigh the documentation gains.
